camelback-echo-canyon.note: Echo Canyon Trail closes 8am to 5pm daily under the City of Phoenix Trail Heat Safety Program while the National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for the Phoenix metro area remains in effect, through July 29, 2026 at 8pm. Source: City of Phoenix Parks and Recreation.

camelback-cholla.note: Cholla Trail closes 8am to 5pm daily under the City of Phoenix Trail Heat Safety Program while the National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for the Phoenix metro area remains in effect, through July 29, 2026 at 8pm. Cholla Trail is also scheduled to close entirely for construction from August 10 through August 21, 2026; Echo Canyon Trailhead will be the alternate access point during that closure. Source: City of Phoenix Parks and Recreation.

white-tank-waterfall.note: Main Trailhead Staging Area closed for construction through 8/31/26; Waterfall/Ford Canyon Trail remains open but is not reachable from the staging area during the closure. Source: Maricopa County Parks and Recreation. A National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning is also active for the Phoenix metro area, in effect through July 29, 2026 at 8pm; hike only in early morning hours and carry extra water. browns-ranch.note: Brown's Ranch Trailhead (building, parking lot, and portions of the surrounding trail system) closed since July 13, 2026 for a $1.17 million improvement project; the city expects the work to wrap up by fall 2026. Source: City of Scottsdale McDowell Sonoran Preserve.

thunderbird-h3.note: 59th Avenue Trailhead closed for improvement construction through December 2026; trails remain open but require using the 55th Avenue or 67th Avenue trailheads instead. Source: City of Glendale Parks and Recreation. A National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning is also active for the Phoenix metro area, in effect through July 29, 2026 at 8pm; hike only in early morning hours and carry extra water. Source: National Weather Service.

devils-bridge.note: Both approaches (Dry Creek Road and Mescal Trailhead) remain closed under the Pocket Fire closure order; the fire is at 95 percent containment but the forest closure order remains in effect through September 30, 2026 unless rescinded. Source: Coconino National Forest.

boynton-canyon.note: Access closed at the Dry Creek Road/Boynton Canyon Road junction under the Pocket Fire closure order, in effect through September 30, 2026 unless rescinded. Source: Coconino National Forest.

west-fork-oak-creek.note: Oak Creek Canyon (Call of the Canyon/West Fork) closed under the Pocket Fire closure order, in effect through September 30, 2026 unless rescinded. A separate Oak Creek temporary area closure (Forest Order 03-04-06-26-002) additionally closes a portion of Oak Creek due to flood damage from the Pocket Fire burn scar, in effect through August 3, 2026 at 2400 hours unless rescinded. Source: Coconino National Forest.

soldier-pass.note: Soldier Pass Trailhead closed under the Pocket Fire closure order, in effect through September 30, 2026 unless rescinded. Source: Coconino National Forest.

mescal-courthouse.note: Mescal Trailhead and the Dry Creek Road corridor closed under the Pocket Fire closure order, in effect through September 30, 2026 unless rescinded. Source: Coconino National Forest.

lava-river-cave.note: FR 171, the access road from FR 245 to the Lava River Cave trailhead, is closed to motorized vehicles for maintenance starting July 13, 2026; reaching the cave requires hiking or biking a longer unpaved approach. Source: Coconino National Forest (Forest Order 03-04-08-26-02).

north-kaibab-coconino.note: Stage 3 Water Restrictions remain in effect on the North Rim following an April 2026 pipeline break; Supai Tunnel water and all other North Rim potable water are off, and Manzanita Rest Area is currently the only reliable water source on the upper trail, so hikers must carry all water needed to reach it. A separate hard closure of the trail between Redwall Bridge and Cottonwood Campground for waterline rehabilitation is scheduled to begin October 15, 2026 and continue into 2027. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.
